<h2>📰 News</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>2026-06-01</strong> 🚀 <strong>v0.1.9 released</strong> (<code>pip install -U vibe-trading-ai</code>): Rolls up everything since 0.1.8. Connector-first broker profiles (IBKR local read-only TWS / IB Gateway + Robinhood Agentic Trading behind OAuth, a committed mandate, order guard, audit ledger, and instant halt). Research Goal runtime across CLI / REST / MCP / Web. A swarm pass — live reconcile + MCP keepalive, operator-configured worker MCP tools, a strict alpha-bench random control, and a new <code>retry_run</code> to relaunch failed/stale runs (<strong>36 MCP tools</strong> now). The <code>agent/cli/</code> package refactor with a refreshed terminal UI, the <code>mootdx</code> no-token A-share loader, and a robustness pass across backtest / agent loop / sessions. <code>--version</code> now always matches the installed package, fixing the 0.1.8 drift (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/156" rel="nofollow">#156</a>).</li>
<li><strong>2026-05-31</strong> 🔌 <strong>Connector-first broker architecture (IBKR + Robinhood)</strong>: Trading access now starts from a selectable connector profile instead of separate broker/live entry points. <code>vibe-trading connector list/use/check/account/positions/orders/quote/history</code> and the MCP <code>trading_*</code> tools share the same selected profile, where paper/live is an attribute of the connector. IBKR can be used immediately through a local read-only TWS / IB Gateway profile, while the official IBKR remote MCP path is seeded as an OAuth <code>mcp.read</code> probe until stable read tool names are available. Robinhood Agentic Trading remains the bounded live MCP connector behind OAuth, a committed mandate, order guard, audit ledger, and instant halt.</li>
<li><strong>2026-05-30</strong> 🧰 <strong>Robustness pass — backtest, agent loop, sessions</strong>: LLM-generated signal engines now pass pre-flight interface validation before instantiation, catching circular self-imports, a missing <code>generate()</code>, non-defaulted <code>__init__</code> args, and wrong return types with actionable JSON errors instead of raw tracebacks (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/149" rel="nofollow">#149</a>); a follow-up routes source-level AST validation errors through the same clean JSON envelope. The agent loop no longer burns all 50 iterations into a <code>failed</code> status with no output — it mirrors the swarm worker's wrap-up nudge at 80% of the iteration budget and drops tool definitions on the last iteration to force a final text answer (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/148" rel="nofollow">#148</a>), guarded to fire only mid-run so it never displaces research-goal context. Session message writes now <code>flush + fsync</code> each append so expensive AI responses survive a mid-write crash, and the read path skips corrupted JSONL lines (logging the first 200 chars for recovery) instead of 500-ing the whole <code>/messages</code> endpoint (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/147" rel="nofollow">#147</a>). The Web composer also fixes IME Enter handling so a composition-confirming Enter no longer submits mid-word (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/146" rel="nofollow">#146</a>).</li>
</ul>

<h2>💡 What Is Vibe-Trading?</h2>
<p>Vibe-Trading is an open-source research workspace for turning finance questions into runnable analysis. It connects natural-language prompts to market-data loaders, strategy generation, backtest engines, reports, exports, and persistent research memory.</p>
<p>It is designed for research, simulation, and backtesting — and, when you choose, autonomous trading through a broker you authorize yourself (e.g. Robinhood Agentic Trading). It holds no funds and never trades outside the limits you set, and you can halt it instantly.</p>

<h3>Security defaults</h3>
<p>For localhost development, <code>vibe-trading serve</code> keeps the browser workflow simple. For any non-local client, sensitive API endpoints require <code>API_AUTH_KEY</code>; use <code>Authorization: Bearer <key></code> for JSON/upload requests. Browser EventSource streams are handled by the Web UI after you enter the same key once in Settings.</p>
<p>Shell-capable tools are available to local CLI and trusted localhost workflows, but are not exposed to remote API sessions unless you explicitly set <code>VIBE_TRADING_ENABLE_SHELL_TOOLS=1</code>. Document and journal readers are limited to upload/import roots by default; place files under <code>agent/uploads</code>, <code>agent/runs</code>, <code>./uploads</code>, <code>./data</code>, <code>~/.vibe-trading/uploads</code>, or <code>~/.vibe-trading/imports</code>, or add a dedicated directory through <code>VIBE_TRADING_ALLOWED_FILE_ROOTS</code>.</p>
<h3>Web UI Settings</h3>
<p>The Web UI Settings page lets local users update the LLM provider/model, base URL, generation parameters, reasoning effort, and optional market data credentials such as the Tushare token. Settings are persisted to <code>agent/.env</code>; provider defaults are loaded from <code>agent/src/providers/llm_providers.json</code>.</p>

If <code>API_AUTH_KEY</code> is unset for dev mode, settings access is accepted only from loopback clients.</p>

<h3>Tool naming</h3>
<p>Ordinary remote tools are exposed with stable names: <code>mcp_<server>_<tool></code>.
Live-broker MCP servers stay behind the <code>trading_*</code> connector surface.</p>
<p>If two server names produce the same ASCII-safe local prefix (e.g. <code>foo-bar</code> and <code>foo_bar</code> both become <code>foo_bar</code>), a deterministic hash suffix is appended at the server-segment level so names remain unique. The operator receives a warning:</p>
<pre><code>WARNING: Configured MCP server 'foo-bar' collides with another server after local name
normalization. Using local tool prefix 'mcp_foo_bar_<hash>_<tool>' to keep generated
tool names unique. Rename the server in agent config if you want a different prefix.
</code></pre>
